name: Open folio
rationale: An open record, not a new institution. Retains the book cue already used by Portal; the quiet sage binding and coral tab belong to the approved illustrations.

name: Doorway P
rationale: A geometric P is also an open doorway. A strong small-size alternative for a front-desk-led identity.

name: Card index
rationale: Three offset index cards make an identifiable corner. Useful when records, rather than a book, should lead the identity.

name: Reading lamp
rationale: A task lamp: practical illumination rather than a badge. Warmer and more illustrative than the other proposals.

name: Key record
rationale: A compact key with a record-card bow. An authentication-centered option; less suited to a whole academic product.

name: Term compass
rationale: Four folded leaves face the center. Academic orientation without a literal navigation arrow.

name: Folded P
rationale: The corner of one sheet folds into a P-shaped silhouette. A more abstract, high-contrast document mark.

name: Handoff
rationale: Two overlapping sheets share a common edge. Emphasizes the student-to-advisor handover.

name: Courtyard
rationale: Three arches around a shared opening. Architectural without copying a university seal or campus facade.

name: Sewn register
rationale: Visible stitching gives a record book a human, maintained quality. A quiet alternate to the open-book mark.

name: Learning path
rationale: One continuous route connects a small set of course points. Expresses a planned path rather than a performance dashboard.

name: Study window
rationale: An uneven four-pane study window. Calm, compact and intentionally different from the book vocabulary.

name: Stepped portal
rationale: Nested right-angle thresholds create a clear opening. The most architectural and least illustrative proposal.

name: Advising pair
rationale: Two compact speech slips create a shared center. A communication-led mark; best used only when advising is the product emphasis.

name: Ribbon initial
rationale: One folded ribbon makes a P. Confident at favicon scale, but less obviously academic than the recommendation.
